observations.text: SP, due to a descent planning technique that started the letdown on visual estimation instead of the TACAN DME to the VFR entry point, did not carry out the pre-descent procedures and checks in time and did not achieve the assigned altitude before the entry point. The formation crossed the authorized entry point 400 feet above the assigned altitude and 25 knots fast, with the result that the IP directed the level-off and passed the corrected descent point. Repetition of the return profile against defined DME and altitude gates is required.

SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the aircraft's position in the pattern, did not remain cognizant of the authorized VFR entry points and did not direct the formation in time to the entry point. The inbound heading was 15 degrees off the published track and the assigned altitude was exceeded by 400 feet, with the result that the IP took over the lead radio calls and directed the repositioning of the formation. Re-establishing the position picture with VOR/DME, TACAN or GPS before commencing the descent is required.

SP directed the formation to the authorized VFR entry point and entered the air traffic pattern within the desired standards for this training block, completing the pre-descent procedures and checks after the IP's verbal indications and without any IP control input. The assigned altitude was held to 300 feet and the airspeed to 20 knots at the entry point, with the deviations recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - the prompts were required only on the first two ATC directives, and earlier initiation of the pre-descent checks is expected to improve the accuracy at the entry point.

SP departed the assigned flight area according to ATC instructions and approached the authorized VFR entry point without the IP's verbal indications. Minor errors in the descent profile produced altitude deviations of 200 feet, airspeed deviations of 15 knots and an inbound heading 8 degrees off the published track, all recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner without IP's intervention. The wingman was placed on the correct side for the BREAK and the formation was directed to the BREAK of the active RWY. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP directed the formation in time to the authorized VFR entry point, carried out the pre-descent procedures and checks with accuracy and speed, and achieved the assigned altitude before the entry point. TACAN and GPS were used to remain orientated with the airport environment, with altitude held within 100 feet, airspeed within 7 knots and the inbound heading within 4 degrees. ATC directives were followed without misapprehensions and the wingman was placed in the correct position for the BREAK of the active RWY. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned and executed the return, descent and traffic pattern entry with exceptional accuracy, anticipating each ATC directive and completing the pre-descent procedures and checks well before the authorized VFR entry point. Deviations were negligible, with the assigned altitude held within 50 feet, the airspeed within 3 knots and the inbound heading within 2 degrees. The wingman was placed in the correct position for the BREAK, the formation was directed to the BREAK of the active RWY and the landing pattern procedures of the LAPs were applied without any IP input. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a return technique that left the airspeed reduction until after the descent had been established, did not carry out the pre-descent procedures and checks before reaching the authorized VFR entry point. The formation arrived at the entry point 30 knots fast and 400 feet above the assigned altitude, with the result that the IP directed the deceleration and executed part of the pattern entry. Repetition of the descent and deceleration sequence against the LAP altitude and airspeed gates is required.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, with navigation, communication and formation control attempted simultaneously, did not follow the ATC directives without misapprehensions and did not use TACAN or GPS to remain orientated with the airport environment. The formation was led past the authorized VFR entry point with the inbound heading 15 degrees in error, with the result that the IP took the radio and directed the re-entry. Shedding the secondary tasks and completing the pre-descent checks before the letdown is required.

SP, due to a lead scan that concentrated on the wingman's position instead of the control and performance instruments during the letdown, did not achieve the assigned altitude before the authorized VFR entry point. The altitude at the entry point was 300 feet off and the airspeed 20 knots off, corrected only after the IP's verbal indications and with delay, without any IP control input. Alternating the lead scan between the wingman and the flight instruments during the descent is required.

SP, due to an unstandard read-back that did not confirm the actual clearance, did not follow the ATC directives without misapprehensions and turned the formation toward an entry point other than the one assigned. The error was recognized with delay after the IP's verbal indications, and the correct entry point was reached with the assigned altitude 300 feet off and the inbound heading 10 degrees off the published track. No IP control input was required. Standard read-back of the entry point and of the assigned altitude before the descent is required.

SP directed the formation to the authorized VFR entry point and entered the air traffic pattern within the desired standards for this training block, applying the pre-descent procedures and checks without IP's intervention. Minor errors produced altitude deviations of 200 feet, airspeed deviations of 15 knots and an inbound heading 8 degrees off the published track, all recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section - the corrections were applied close to the entry point rather than during the letdown, and earlier initiation of the descent is expected to improve the accuracy at the entry point.

SP departed the assigned flight area as determined in the LAP, directed the formation in time to the authorized VFR entry point and achieved the assigned altitude before it. TACAN and DME were used throughout the return to remain orientated with the airport environment, with altitude held within 100 feet, airspeed within 7 knots and the inbound heading within 4 degrees. ATC directives were followed without misapprehensions, the wingman was placed in the correct position for the BREAK and the formation was directed to the BREAK of the active RWY with accuracy and speed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP anticipated the recovery sequence, completed the pre-descent procedures and checks early and directed the formation to the authorized VFR entry point without a single repetition of an ATC directive. Deviations were negligible, with the assigned altitude held within 50 feet, the airspeed within 3 knots and the inbound heading within 2 degrees. The wingman was placed in the correct position for the BREAK and the landing pattern procedures of the LAPs were applied with exceptional accuracy. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a descent profile flown without altitude and distance gates, did not complete the pre-descent procedures and checks and did not achieve the assigned altitude before the authorized VFR entry point. The formation crossed the entry point 400 feet high with the airspeed 25 knots above the briefed value, with the result that the IP directed the correction and executed part of the pattern entry. Repetition of the return profile with defined DME and altitude gates is required.

SP, due to lack of awareness of the aircraft's position relative to the area boundary, did not depart the assigned flight area at the point determined in the LAP and did not approach the authorized VFR entry point. The inbound heading was 20 degrees off the published track and the assigned altitude was exceeded by 500 feet, with the result that the IP took the lead of the formation and directed the recovery to the correct entry point. Use of VOR/DME, TACAN or GPS for the area exit and for orientation with the airport environment is required.

SP, due to a pre-descent check flow that was started only after the ATC descent clearance had been received, did not achieve the assigned altitude before the authorized VFR entry point. The altitude at the entry point was 300 feet off and the airspeed 20 knots off, corrected after the IP's verbal indications and with delay, without any IP control input. Anticipation of the descent clearance and completion of the checks before the letdown is required.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on the recovery track, did not remain cognizant of the entry points and of the approach procedure and did not place the wingman on the correct side for the BREAK. The formation reached the entry point with the assigned altitude 300 feet off and the inbound heading 10 degrees off the published track, corrected with delay after the IP's verbal indications. Re-establishing the position picture and the formation geometry after each transmission is required.

SP, due to a descent rate that was reduced late in the letdown, did not achieve the assigned altitude before reaching the authorized VFR entry point at the briefed airspeed. The altitude at the entry point was 200 feet off and the airspeed 15 knots off, recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner without IP's intervention. The wingman was placed in the correct position for the BREAK and the formation was directed to the BREAK of the active RWY.

SP, due to an incomplete mental model of the approach sequence that was not updated when the clearance changed, did not follow the revised ATC directive to the second entry point at the first transmission. The inbound heading was 8 degrees off the published track and the assigned altitude 200 feet off when the correction was applied, recognized and corrected by the SP in a timely manner without IP's intervention. The remainder of the pattern entry and the placement of the wingman for the BREAK were carried out as briefed.

SP directed the formation in time to the authorized VFR entry point, carried out the pre-descent procedures and checks and achieved the assigned altitude before the entry point, within the desired standards for this training block. Altitude was held within 120 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and the inbound heading within 4 degrees, with all corrections applied without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - the deviations were at the upper end of the desired band on the first recovery and reduced on the second, and a more regular use of TACAN and DME during the letdown is expected to improve the accuracy at the entry point.

SP planned the recovery from the assigned flight area with exceptional accuracy, anticipated every ATC directive and completed the pre-descent procedures and checks well before the authorized VFR entry point. The assigned altitude was held within 50 feet, the airspeed within 3 knots and the inbound heading within 2 degrees throughout the descent and the traffic pattern entry. The wingman was placed in the correct position for the BREAK, the formation was directed to the BREAK of the active RWY and the landing pattern procedures of the LAPs were applied without any IP input. Above end of block MIF achieved.
